preamble: The change of the labiodental [f] to the dental [θ] is far rarer than the reverse change, TH-fronting (θ > f). Blevins (2019) finds no clear case of a regular, context-free f > θ. The forms that are attested are sporadic substitutions in Spanish varieties with both /f/ and /θ/: Celipe for Felipe in Castilla la Nueva, and [ˈgaθas] for gafas in Equatorial Guinea. They are best explained as misperception or as hypercorrection against the more frequent θ > f substitution in the same varieties.

examples.note: Found among speakers with little schooling (Moreno Fernández 1996, cited in Blevins 2019); sporadic, not a regular change.
Reported 'with some frequency' alongside the opposite substitution θ > f, as in [ˈfelja] for Celia (Quilis 1996, cited in Blevins 2019).

sources: Blevins, J. (2019). Deconstructing markedness in sound change typology: Notes on θ > f and f > θ. In Perspectives on Language Structure and Language Change, Current Issues in Linguistic Theory 345. John Benjamins. https://doi.org/10.1075/cilt.345.04ble
